New --project-description PATH CLI flag on verify_production_security_profile.py; omitting it skips the version check entirely (backward compatible with every existing invocation, including the sdkconfig-only RepositoryLayeredProfileTest simulation which has no real build directory).

policy_question_resolved.status: COMPLETE -- by explicit user decision, not assumed
policy_question_resolved.detail: Asked the user directly (AskUserQuestion) which rule the verifier should enforce, given the real, previously-documented discrepancy: exact 5.5.2 (matching the plan's literal text), any 5.5.x (matching this project's actual release-v5.5-tracking CI), update the plan's own pin to 5.5.5, or defer the decision further. User chose 'allow any 5.5.x'. Implemented exactly that -- MAJOR.MINOR pinned, PATCH unconstrained.

dependencies_lock_discrepancy_found.detail: While capturing the real project_description.json fixture, `idf.py reconfigure`'s Component Manager step rewrote this repository's own git-tracked dependencies.lock (`idf: version: 5.5.2` -> `5.5.5`) as a side effect -- an independent, build-verified confirmation that the plan's originally written 5.5.2 pin is not just prose but also exists in a tracked repo file, and that a real build already disagrees with it. Reverted via `git checkout -- dependencies.lock` before finishing (this project's established Docker-artifact-cleanup discipline, see [[esp-idf-available-via-docker]]) -- updating a git-tracked lock file is a separate, reviewable change not folded into this pass.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: The version check enforces MAJOR.MINOR==5.5 with any PATCH, not exactly 5.5.2 as the plan's literal text states.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: The user explicitly resolved this previously-flagged, previously-deferred policy discrepancy (docs/security/PRODUCTION_HARDENING.md Section 2.3 from the prior sub-slice) by choosing 'allow any 5.5.x' when asked directly -- this project's actual CI configuration (espressif/idf:release-v5.5, a branch-tracking tag) has never resolved to exactly 5.5.2 in this sandbox, so an exact-5.5.2 check would fail this project's own real CI image on every run.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: A production build using a genuinely different, non-5.5.x ESP-IDF major/minor (e.g. an accidental 5.6.0 or 6.0.0 toolchain) is caught; a build using 5.5.2 vs. 5.5.5 vs. any other 5.5.x patch is not distinguished, matching what the user decided is actually meaningful for this project.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: dependencies.lock's own independent `idf: version: 5.5.2` pin (a git-tracked Component Manager lock entry, separate from the plan's prose and from verify_production_security_profile.py's now-implemented check) was found to disagree with the real toolchain in use, but was not updated in this pass.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Updating a git-tracked lock file is a distinct, independently-reviewable change (it affects what the ESP-IDF Component Manager considers a version drift on every future build, not just this verifier's diagnostic), and this sub-slice's explicit scope (per the user's selected AskUserQuestion option) was the verifier's version check, not a general audit of every place an ESP-IDF version might be pinned in this repository.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: A real `idf.py reconfigure`/`build` run against this repository's real dependencies.lock will continue to want to rewrite it to 5.5.5 until someone deliberately updates the file (or repins the Component Manager dependency differently); this sandbox's real-build passes must keep reverting it via `git checkout` afterward.
